title: Fuels & combustion
examples: What is the difference between complete and incomplete combustion?
What kinds of pollutants are released when fuels burn?
How can we reduce air pollution from burning fuels?

explain.say: Today we will learn about fuels and how they burn.
Combustion is a chemical reaction that releases energy.
Complete combustion happens when there is plenty of oxygen available.
Incomplete combustion happens when oxygen supply is limited.
Carbon monoxide is a very dangerous pollutant gas.
When burning wood indoors without ventilation, you risk CO buildup.

faq.q: Why is carbon monoxide so dangerous to breathe?
faq.a: Carbon monoxide binds to haemoglobin in your blood much more strongly than oxygen does. This prevents your blood from carrying enough oxygen to your body's organs.
asks: What happens if I breathe CO?

faq.q: What is the difference between the products of complete and incomplete burning?
faq.a: Complete burning always produces carbon dioxide and water. Incomplete burning produces carbon monoxide and solid carbon, which is soot.
asks: What do you get when fuel burns badly?
Can you list the products of combustion?

faq.q: Are all pollutants harmful to the environment?
faq.a: Some pollutants are harmful, like sulphur dioxide, which causes acid rain. However, the impact depends on the concentration and type of pollutant.
asks: Are all gases from burning bad?

faq.q: Do I need to worry about pollutants in my daily life?
faq.a: Yes, vehicle exhaust and burning fossil fuels release many pollutants. Good ventilation helps reduce indoor pollutant buildup.
asks: How can I keep my air clean?

faq.q: What is the role of oxygen in combustion?
faq.a: Oxygen acts as the oxidising agent, meaning it is necessary for the fuel to burn. Without oxygen, combustion cannot happen.
asks: Must oxygen be present for burning?
What is the role of oxygen in a fire?

facts: Complete combustion of a hydrocarbon yields only carbon dioxide and water.
Incomplete combustion produces carbon monoxide and unburnt carbon (soot).
Sulphur dioxide is a major pollutant released from burning sulphur-containing fuels.
Carbon monoxide is colourless and odourless, making it particularly dangerous.

quiz.say: When burning fuel with limited oxygen, what pollutant is mainly produced?
quiz.why: Limited oxygen causes the reaction to be incomplete, resulting in CO production.

wrong.0: Soot is also produced, but carbon monoxide is the primary, most dangerous gaseous pollutant.
wrong.2: This is the product of complete combustion, which needs plenty of oxygen.
wrong.3: Water is always a product, but it does not indicate the type of combustion.

quiz.say: Which condition leads to the production of carbon dioxide and water?
quiz.why: Having sufficient oxygen ensures the reaction burns fully, producing only CO2 and H2O.

wrong.0: Sulphur adds SO2, but the main difference is the oxygen level.
wrong.2: High temperature is needed, but oxygen supply is the determining factor for product type.
wrong.3: A closed container might limit oxygen, causing incomplete combustion.

quiz.say: If a fire has poor ventilation, what is the most likely pollutant hazard?
quiz.why: Poor ventilation means low oxygen, leading to incomplete combustion and high CO levels.

wrong.0: SO2 comes from sulphur in the fuel, not just poor ventilation.
wrong.1: CO2 is a normal product, but high levels are dangerous from lack of oxygen.
wrong.2: While soot is present, the invisible and highly toxic gas is the main danger.
